advances:
This proves a directional Bonnesen-type lower bound for the mixed area
in the accepted common-plane gate.  In the normalized simplex frame,
the \(Q_1,Q_2\) centroid separation forces a directional width ratio at
least \(\Lambda=\max\{A,B\}>1\).  Exact equal-width section
integration then gives
\[
2V(P,C)\ge p\Lambda+\frac{\sigma}{\Lambda}.
\]
Combining this with the quantitative \(\Gamma\)-bridge produces one
explicit affine-invariant lower bound for both the hull area and its
weighted \(R^\star\)-charge.  The three tails turn it into two
checkable general classes, one forcing \(k>M+m\) and one forcing
\(W^\star>0\).  This is not a ratio-only claim: parallel rectangles
attain the directional mixed-area inequality exactly for every width
ratio, so the scalar relaxation and thin-strip geometries do not
falsify it and do not automatically satisfy either closing condition.
author: mp_r375_triplehull_abstract
proof:
We first prove the directional mixed-area inequality used below. Let \(K,L\) be planar convex bodies, let \(\varphi\) be a nonconstant affine functional, and write \[ w_\varphi(E)=\max_E\varphi-\min_E\varphi. \] Set \[ r=\frac{w_\varphi(L)}{w_\varphi(K)}>0. \] Then \[ 2V(K,L)\ge r|K|+\frac{|L|}{r}. \tag{10} \] To prove (10), first suppose the two \(\varphi\)-widths are equal. Translate the bodies so that both \(\varphi\)-projections are the same interval \(I\). Choose an affine functional \(\psi\) whose linear part is independent of that of \(\varphi\). In the \((\varphi,\psi)\)-plane, the section of each body over \(t\in I\) is an interval. Denote the two section lengths, in the common \(\psi\)-coordinate, by \(\ell_K(t)\) and \(\ell_L(t)\). For \(0\le s\le1\), the section of \((1-s)K+sL\) over the same \(t\) contains \[ (1-s)K_t+sL_t, \] whose length is \[ (1-s)\ell_K(t)+s\ell_L(t). \] Integrating over \(I\), with the same constant Jacobian for both bodies, gives \[ |(1-s)K+sL| \ge(1-s)|K|+s|L|. \tag{11} \] The mixed-area polynomial gives \[ |(1-s)K+sL| =(1-s)^2|K|+2s(1-s)V(K,L)+s^2|L|. \tag{12} \] Subtracting the right side of (11) from (12) and dividing by \(s(1-s)>0\) proves \[ 2V(K,L)\ge|K|+|L| \] in the equal-width case. For general \(r\), translate \(L\) arbitrarily and apply a uniform homothety of ratio \(1/r\), obtaining \(L'\). Then \[ w_\varphi(L')=w_\varphi(K),\qquad |L'|=\frac{|L|}{r^2},\qquad V(K,L')=\frac{V(K,L)}r. \] The equal-width inequality for \(K,L'\), multiplied by \(r\), is exactly (10). Return to \(P,C\). Define the normalized affine simplex coordinates \[ \xi_i(x)=\frac{f_i(x)-L_i}{\Delta}. \] On \(P\), one has \(\xi_i\ge0\) and \(\xi_1+\xi_2+\xi_3=1\). Hence \[ w_{\xi_1}(P)\le1,\qquad w_{\xi_2}(P)\le1. \tag{13} \] Because \(y_1,y_2\in C\), their coordinate differences give \[ w_{\xi_1}(C) \ge \xi_1(y_2)-\xi_1(y_1)=A, \] \[ w_{\xi_2}(C) \ge \xi_2(y_1)-\xi_2(y_2)=B. \tag{14} \] Choose \(i\in\{1,2\}\) attaining \(\Lambda=\max\{A,B\}\), and put \[ r=\frac{w_{\xi_i}(C)}{w_{\xi_i}(P)}. \] The body \(P\) has positive area, so its \(\xi_i\)-width is positive. Equations (13)--(14) give \[ r\ge\Lambda>1. \tag{15} \] Convexity of \(A_2\) gives \(C\subseteq A_2\), so \[ \sigma\le m

0. \] Apply (10) with \(K=P,L=C,\varphi=\xi_i\), and then use (15): \[ 2V(P,C)\ge g(r)\ge g(\Lambda) =p\Lambda+\frac{\sigma}{\Lambda}. \] This proves (3). The proof also shows directly that (3) is invariant under every nonsingular affine change of the common plane: widths in the pulled-back functional have the same ratio, while all areas and mixed areas scale by the same absolute determinant. Accepted fact `7706987b44b0132f` gives \[ k\ge|H| \ge\frac14\bigl(p+\sigma+2V(P,C)\bigr) \tag{17} \] and \[ \mathcal R^\star_K \ge \frac38\bigl(p+\sigma+2V(P,C)\bigr)+\frac72\Gamma. \tag{18} \] Combining (3) with (17) proves (4). Combining (2), (3), and (18) proves the strict bound (5). Here \(\Delta>2\), \(\lambda>1\), and \(d_\alpha\ge1\), so the denominator is positive. A large \(\Delta\) weakens the bridge term, as it must; it is not replaced by a false uniform constant. We next use all three tails. In row \(i\), the crossing equality and the left tail give \[ h=u_i+v_i+c_i,\qquad c_i+m\ge h, \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad u_i+v_i\le m. \tag{19} \] Under the exact \(Q\)-support, \[ v_1=m-b,\qquad v_2=m-a,\qquad v_3=q. \] Substitution in (19) gives (6). The sets \(Q_1,Q_2\) are disjoint up to null cutting lines and lie in \(C\), so \[ \sigma\ge a+b\ge U. \tag{20} \] Moreover, \[ \mathcal Q^\star =\frac32(a+b)+5\gamma+7q \ge\frac32(a+b)\ge\frac32U, \] while the third inequality in (6) gives \[ \mathcal Q^\star \ge\frac32(a+b+\gamma)\ge\frac32u_3. \] This proves (7). Since \(m

M+m. \] Under (9), inequalities (5) and (7) give \[ \mathcal R^\star_K > 2p-\mathcal P^\star-\underline{\mathcal Q} \ge 2p-\mathcal P^\star-\mathcal Q^\star. \] Accepted fact `7706987b44b0132f` supplies the exact common-level identity \[ W^\star =-2p+\mathcal P^\star+\mathcal Q^\star+\mathcal R^\star_K, \] so \(W^\star>0\), proving (9). Finally, (10) survives the scalar and thin-strip tests sharply. For arbitrary \(p,\sigma,r,R>0\), take \[ P_R=[0,R]\times\left[0,\frac pR\right], \qquad C_R=[0,rR]\times\left[0,\frac{\sigma}{rR}\right], \] and use horizontal projection. The width ratio is exactly \(r\), and \[ P_R+C_R =[0,(1+r)R]\times \left[0,\frac pR+\frac{\sigma}{rR}\right]. \] Consequently \[ |P_R+C_R| =p+\sigma+pr+\frac{\sigma}{r}, \] so \[ 2V(P_R,C_R)=pr+\frac{\sigma}{r}. \] The aspect ratio \(R^2/p\) may be arbitrarily large. Thus no stronger directional lower bound follows from the area data and one width ratio, and neither (8) nor (9) is silently implied by a scalar table lacking the required common-plane width profile.
statement:
Assume all hypotheses and notation of accepted facts
`7706987b44b0132f` and `05153059dfd604c8`.  Thus the full canonical
single-double hypotheses hold, including all three actual lower
crossings, all three crossing equalities, finite interior, both tails
in every row, \(W=0\), and
\[
\{J:q_J>0\}=\{123,1,2,12\}.
\]
Write
\[
p=p_\varnothing,\qquad
a=q_1,\qquad b=q_2,\qquad
\gamma=q_{12},\qquad q=q_{123},
\]
\[
m=a+b+\gamma+q,\qquad
\Delta=-1-(L_1+L_2+L_3),
\]
and put
\[
\beta=\frac{93+12\sqrt{21}}{50}.
\]
Accepted fact `05153059dfd604c8` gives
\[
\frac pm>\beta>1,\qquad \Delta>2.
\tag{1}
\]

Use the notation of accepted fact `7706987b44b0132f`:
\[
P=\overline{P_\varnothing},\qquad
C=\operatorname{conv}(\overline{Q_1}\cup\overline{Q_2}),
\qquad \sigma=|C|,
\]
\[
|P+C|=p+\sigma+2V(P,C),
\]
\[
\Gamma=\left|
\operatorname{conv}\left(
\frac{P+\overline{Q_1}}2\cup
\frac{P+\overline{Q_2}}2
\right)\cap R_{12}\right|.
\]
With the notation of accepted fact `f1fcc678305bbd1c`, set
\[
\mathcal T_P=\{f_i>L_i:\ i=1,2,3\},\qquad
\Theta=|\mathcal T_P|,\qquad
\alpha=\frac p\Theta,
\]
let \(y_1,y_2\) be the area centroids of \(Q_1,Q_2\), and define
\[
A=\frac{(f_1+L_1)(y_2)-(f_1+L_1)(y_1)}{\Delta},
\]
\[
B=\frac{(f_2+L_2)(y_1)-(f_2+L_2)(y_2)}{\Delta},
\]
\[
\Lambda=\max\{A,B\},\qquad
\lambda=\min\{A,B\},\qquad
d_\alpha=1+\sqrt{1-\alpha}.
\]
Then
\[
0<\alpha\le1,\qquad A,B>1,
\qquad
\Gamma>\frac{p\Lambda}{\Delta\lambda d_\alpha}.
\tag{2}
\]

The following directional mixed-area inequality holds:
\[
\boxed{\qquad
2V(P,C)\ge p\Lambda+\frac{\sigma}{\Lambda}.
\qquad}
\tag{3}
\]
Consequently the common three-body hull \(H\subseteq K\) and the middle
charge satisfy
\[
\boxed{\qquad
k\ge|H|
\ge
\frac14\left(
p(1+\Lambda)+
\sigma\left(1+\frac1\Lambda\right)
\right),
\qquad}
\tag{4}
\]
\[
\boxed{\qquad
\mathcal R^\star_K
>
\frac38\left(
p(1+\Lambda)+
\sigma\left(1+\frac1\Lambda\right)
\right)
+\frac{7p\Lambda}{2\Delta\lambda d_\alpha}.
\qquad}
\tag{5}
\]

All three tails give the simultaneous consequences
\[
u_1\le b,\qquad
u_2\le a,\qquad
u_3\le a+b+\gamma.
\tag{6}
\]
Put
\[
U=u_1+u_2,\qquad
\underline{\mathcal Q}
=\frac32\max\{U,u_3\}.
\]
Then
\[
\sigma\ge U,\qquad
\mathcal Q^\star\ge\underline{\mathcal Q}.
\tag{7}
\]
Therefore the following are two nontrivial general classes closed by
the directional profile:
\[
p(1+\Lambda)+
U\left(1+\frac1\Lambda\right)
\ge
4\left(M+\frac p\beta\right)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
k>M+m,
\tag{8}
\]
\[
\frac38\left(
p(1+\Lambda)+
U\left(1+\frac1\Lambda\right)
\right)
+\frac{7p\Lambda}{2\Delta\lambda d_\alpha}
\ge
2p-\mathcal P^\star-\underline{\mathcal Q}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
W^\star>0.
\tag{9}
\]
The full common-level hypotheses give \(W^\star=W=0\), so (9) is
impossible.  Every term in (3)--(9) is affine invariant after the
common area normalization.
